concrete_cover.title: Nominal Concrete Cover for Durability
concrete_cover.description: Minimum clear distance from concrete surface to outermost reinforcement bar to protect steel from environmental ingress.
concrete_cover.keywords: concrete cover clear durability corrosion crack width water tank bridge marine

standards.limits:
Mild: 20mm | Moderate: 30mm | Severe: 45mm | Very Severe: 50mm | Extreme: 75mm.
Note: Liquid-retaining faces in IS 3370 require a flat minimum of 45mm cover.
standards.notation:
**c_nom**: Nominal cover on drawings
**c_min**: Minimum cover for exposure class (IS 456 Table 16)
**Δc_dev**: Execution deviation tolerance (typically 0mm in design office drawings).
standards.notes: Standard prescriptive lookup.

standards.limits:
Moderate: 40mm (In-situ) / 35mm (Precast)
Severe: 45mm (In-situ) / 40mm (Precast)
Very Severe: 50mm (In-situ) / 45mm (Precast)
Extreme: 75mm (In-situ) / 65mm (Precast)
standards.notation:
**c_nom**: Total nominal cover
**c_min,dur**: Minimum durability cover (Table 14.2)
**Δc_dur,γ, Δc_dur,st, Δc_dur,add**: Modification factors for safety element, stainless steel usage, and additional coatings respectively (Clause 14.1.3)
**Δc_dev**: Execution variance allowance (Clause 14.1.4).
standards.notes: Allows adjustments based on manufacturing quality control.

standards.limits:
Mapped by Structural Class (S1-S6) vs Exposure (XC/XD/XS):
• **XC1**: 15mm (S4) / 25mm (S6)
• **XC2/XC3**: 20mm (S4) / 30mm (S6)
• **XC4**: 25mm (S4) / 35mm (S6)
• **XD1/XS1**: 30mm (S4) / 40mm (S6)
• **XD2/XS2**: 35mm (S4) / 45mm (S6)
• **XD3/XS3**: 40mm (S4) / 50mm (S6)
standards.notation:
**c_nom**: Target nominal drawing cover
**c_min**: Minimum concrete cover ($$\max\{c_{min,b}; c_{min,dur}; 10\text{mm}\}$$ per Clause 4.4.1.2)
**Δc_dev**: Execution variance allowance (standard 10mm per Clause 4.4.1.3).
standards.notes: Rigorous lifecycle exposure matrix scaling.

standards.limits:
• **Cast against earth**: 3 in (75mm)
• **Exposed to weather**: 2 in (50mm) for #6 to #18 bars; 1.5 in (38mm) for #5 or smaller.
• **Not exposed**: Slabs/Walls: 0.75 in (20mm) for ≤#11. Beams/Columns: 1.5 in (38mm).
standards.notation: **No variables available**: Uses static, flat prescriptive table data lookup limits instead.
standards.notes: Prescriptive, static dimensional limits.

standards.limits: Calculated dynamically based on target structural reliability index ($$\beta = 1.5\text{ to }3.8$$) mapped against carbonation/chloride diffusion models.
standards.notation:
**P(t)**: Probability of corrosion initiation at time $t$
**c_nom**: Nominal target cover
**x(t)**: Penetration depth of carbonation/chlorides at time $t$
**P_{target}**: Target reliability threshold index limit.
standards.notes: Probabilistic performance-based durability design.

shell_buckling.title: Steel Shell Buckling Stability
shell_buckling.description: Buckling checks for thin-walled cylindrical or conical steel shells under axial compression, bending, and shear load conditions.
shell_buckling.keywords: steel buckling shell local buckling shell stability imperfection tower cylinder pipe container

standards.limits: Classifies tubular members based on diameter-to-thickness ($$d/t$$) ratios. Semi-compact limit is $$d/t \le 88\epsilon^2$$. Beyond this, the section is slender and requires elastic shell theory check.
standards.notation:
**σ_cr**: Critical local buckling stress capacity
**d / t**: Outer diameter / Wall thickness of shell
**E**: Modulus of elasticity ($$2 \times 10^5\text{ MPa}$$)
**μ**: Poisson's ratio (0.3).
standards.notes: Prescriptive geometric limits for standard pipe profiles.

standards.limits: Evaluates meridional, hoop, and shear stresses against buckling boundaries. Scales capacity via fabrication tolerance classes (Class A, B, or C) using a knock-down factor ($$\chi_{ov}$$).
standards.notation:
**σ_x,Ed**: Design meridional stress value
**σ_x,Rd**: Design buckling resistance stress capacity limit
**χ_x**: Buckling reduction factor derived from relative shell slenderness (Clause 8.3)
**f_yk**: Yield strength of steel grade
**γ_M1**: Partial safety factor for resistance to buckling (Section 4).
standards.notes: Rigorous framework linking capacity to fabrication quality tolerances.

standards.clause: Chapter E (Sec E6) & Chapter H (Sec H1.1)
standards.limits: Limits local buckling in round HSS sections via hard geometric boundaries ($$D/t \le 0.45 E / f_y$$). Slender sections exceeding this limit must use reduced critical stress equations.
standards.notation:
**F_cr**: Critical local buckling stress value
**D / t**: Outside diameter / Wall thickness parameter
**E / f_y**: Modulus of elasticity ($$29,000\text{ ksi}$$) / Yield stress.
standards.notes: Simple prescriptive lookup for hollow structural sections.

standards.limits: Evaluates shell stability under combined loading interactions via a utilization capacity limit index. Incorporates specialized knock-down curves accounting for large structural shell imperfections.
standards.notation:
**σ_xd, σ_θd, τ_d**: Design axial, hoop, and shear stresses respectively
**σ_cx, σ_cθ, τ_c**: Buckling strengths under isolated loads (Sec 3.2.2)
**α_1, α_2, α_3**: Structural interaction exponents (Sec 3.2.1 display variables).
standards.notes: Industry benchmark standard for heavy thin-walled shell components.

standards.limits: Enforces non-linear numerical safety checks (GNIA - Geometrically Nonlinear Analysis with Imperfections). Maps geometric shell manufacturing deviations directly into finite element models.
standards.notation:
**γ_Rk / E_d**: Global structural safety factor / Design loading action matrix
**R_d**: Non-linear structural resistance function calculation
**u / a_init**: Displacements field matrix / Initial geometric imperfection amplitude.
standards.notes: Advanced computational simulation framework.

concrete_breakout.title: Anchor Bolt Concrete Breakout Strength
concrete_breakout.description: Calculates the concrete tension breakout capacity of anchor bolt groups embedded in concrete foundation structures.
concrete_breakout.keywords: anchor bolt concrete breakout tension foundation base plate embedment attachment anchor group

standards.limits: Core IS 456 lacks an analytical Concrete Capacity Design (CCD) group model for 35-degree breakout cones. Designs default to verifying simple isolated tensile pullout strength based on concrete tensile capacity across the failure surface area.
standards.notation:
**N_nb**: Nominal concrete breakout tension capacity
**f_ct**: Concrete tensile strength calculated as $$0.7 \sqrt{f_{ck}}$$ (Clause 6.2.2)
**A_proj**: Projected surface area of the isolated failure cone boundary.
standards.notes: Lacks an explicit group spacing/eccentricity interactive model; international standards typically govern complex configurations.

standards.limits: Uses Concrete Capacity Design (CCD) method. Calculates group breakout capacity in tension assuming a failure prism projecting at 35 degrees.
standards.notation:
**N_cbg**: Nominal breakout strength of an anchor group in tension
**A_Nc / A_Nco**: Actual vs reference single-anchor projected concrete failure areas (Sec 17.6.2.1)
**ψ_ec,N, ψ_ed,N, ψ_c,N, ψ_cp,N**: Anchor group modification factors for loading eccentricity, edge distances, concrete cracking, and critical splitting boundaries respectively (Sec 17.6.2.3 to 17.6.2.6)
**N_b**: Basic single anchor breakout capacity calculated as $$k_c \lambda_a \sqrt{f'_c} h_{ef}^{1.5}$$ (Sec 17.6.2.2)
**k_c / f'_c / h_ef**: Concrete effectiveness calibration factor / Compressive strength / Effective anchor embedment depth.
standards.notes: Standardized group interaction methodology widely integrated in calculation engines.

standards.limits: Applies a standardized CCD group model evaluating actual failure geometry lines under combined tension actions.
standards.notation:
**N_Rk,c**: Characteristic tension breakout group capacity resistance
**N⁰_Rk,c**: Basic single anchor resistance calculated as $$k_1 \sqrt{f_{ck,cube}} h_{ef}^{1.5}$$ (Clause 7.2.1.4-Eq 7.1)
**A_c,N / A⁰_c,N**: Actual vs reference single anchor failure areas
**ψ_s,N, ψ_re,N, ψ_ec,N, ψ_p,N**: Geometric modification factor constants for edge proximity, structural reinforcement tracking, load eccentricity, and localized shell spalling splitting boundaries respectively (Clauses 7.2.1.4.2 to 7.2.1.4.5)
**k_1 / f_{ck,cube} / h_ef**: Calibration factor / Concrete cube strength / Effective embedment depth parameter.
standards.notes: Standard unified calculation format across European jurisdictions.

standards.limits: Evaluates base static breakout capacity ($N_{Rk,c}$) via standard CCD, then scales for fatigue conditions under high-cycle cyclic structural tension repetitions.
standards.notation:
**N_Rk,c**: Characteristic static concrete breakout resistance capacity
**A_c,N / A⁰_c,N**: Total actual group failure area vs reference single anchor area
**ψ_s,N, ψ_re,N, ψ_ec,N**: Group modification factor profiles for edge distance proximity, structural cracking containment, and load eccentricities respectively (Section 4.1.2)
**k_1 / f_{ck} / h_ef**: Calibration coefficient / Concrete characteristic cylinder strength / Effective bolt embedment depth profile.
standards.notes: Comprehensive model accounting for baseline static mechanics and long-term cyclic adjustments.

minimum_reinforcement.title: Minimum Reinforcement (Tension, Compression, Shear)
minimum_reinforcement.description: Prescriptive minimum steel area thresholds for structural concrete elements to prevent brittle failure, control cracking, and ensure minimum ductility under unpredicted loads.
minimum_reinforcement.keywords: minimum reinforcement area tension compression shear torsion steel ductility crack control

standards.limits:
• **Beams (Tension)**: $$A_{s} \ge \frac{0.85 b d}{f_y}$$
• **Columns (Compression)**: $$0.8\% \le \rho \le 6\%$$ of gross cross-sectional area
• **Shear Links**: $$A_{sv} \ge \frac{0.4 b s_v}{0.87 f_y}$$
standards.notation:
**A_s,min / A_sv**: Minimum area of tension steel / Minimum area of shear reinforcement (stirrups)
**b / d**: Breadth of rectangular web / Effective depth of structural beam
**s_v**: Spacing of shear stirrups along the element length
**f_y**: Characteristic yield strength of steel reinforcement.
standards.notes: Limits established to prevent sudden brittle failure upon initial cracking of the concrete section.

standards.limits:
• **Beams (Tension)**: Greater of $$\frac{3 \sqrt{f'_c}}{f_y} b_w d$$ or $$\frac{200}{f_y} b_w d$$
• **Columns (Compression)**: $$0.01 A_g \le A_{st} \le 0.08 A_g$$
• **Shear Stirrups**: $$A_{v,min} = 0.75 \sqrt{f'_c} \frac{b_w s}{f_{yt}} \ge \frac{50 b_w s}{f_{yt}}$$
standards.notation:
**A_s,min / A_st**: Minimum flexural reinforcement / Total longitudinal compression reinforcement
**A_v,min**: Minimum area of shear reinforcement within spacing s
**f'_c / f_y / f_yt**: Specified concrete compressive strength (psi) / Yield strength of longitudinal steel / Yield strength of transverse steel
**b_w / d / s**: Web width / Effective depth / Transverse stirrup spacing
**A_g**: Gross cross-sectional area of concrete member.
standards.notes: Tension minimums are directly scaled by the specific concrete strength to match the uncracked section cracking moment.

standards.limits:
• **Beams (Tension)**: $$A_{s,min} = 0.26 \frac{f_{ctm}}{f_{yk}} b_t d \ge 0.0013 b_t d$$
• **Columns (Compression)**: $$A_{s,min} = \max\left( \frac{0.10 N_{Ed}}{f_{yd}}, 0.002 A_c \right)$$
• **Shear**: $$\rho_w \ge \frac{0.08 \sqrt{f_{ck}}}{f_{yk}}$$
standards.notation:
**A_s,min**: Minimum longitudinal tension reinforcement
**f_ctm / f_yk / f_yd**: Mean concrete tensile strength / Characteristic steel yield strength / Design steel yield strength
**b_t / d**: Mean width of the tension zone / Effective depth
**N_Ed**: Design axial compression force
**A_c**: Gross cross-sectional area of concrete
**ρ_w / f_ck**: Shear reinforcement ratio / Characteristic concrete cylinder compressive strength.
standards.notes: Links minimum area directly to the mean tensile strength of concrete to ensure robust crack control across varying grades.

standards.limits:
• **Flexure (Crack Control)**: Formulated directly around residual tensile strength preventing yield at crack formation.
• **Shear**: $$\rho_w \ge 0.08 \frac{\sqrt{f_{ck}}}{f_{yk}}$$
standards.notation:
**A_s,min**: Minimum reinforcing steel area specifically for crack control limitations
**k_c / k**: Coefficient for stress distribution in the cross section / Coefficient for non-uniform self-equilibrating stresses
**f_ct,eff**: Effective tensile strength of concrete at the expected time of crack formation
**A_ct**: Area of concrete acting within the effective tension zone
**σ_s**: Maximum permitted steel stress immediately after crack formation.
standards.notes: Performance-based minimums focused on the exact physics of crack propagation mechanics rather than empirical geometric ratios.

concrete_properties.title: Concrete Characteristic Strength & Material Definitions
concrete_properties.description: Standardized material strength parameters, characteristic test specimen definitions (Cube vs. Cylinder), and calculated design values across major codes.
concrete_properties.keywords: fck fck_cube fck_cyl fctm fcd fctd strength grade characteristic cylinder cube concrete properties compressive tensile design strength

standards.limits:
• **Specimen Standard**: 150mm Cube tested at 28 days.
• **Standard Grades**: M20, M25, M30, M35, M40, M45, M50.
• **Design Compressive Strength ($$f_{cd}$$)**: $$0.447 f_{ck}$$ (Includes $$0.67$$ size-effect factor and $$\gamma_m = 1.5$$).
• **Flexural Tensile Strength ($$f_{cr}$$)**: $$0.7 \sqrt{f_{ck}}$$ N/mm².
• **Modulus of Elasticity ($$E_c$$)**: $$5000 \sqrt{f_{ck}}$$ N/mm².
standards.notation:
**f_ck**: Characteristic 150mm cube compressive strength at 28 days
**f_cd**: Design axial compressive strength for flexure/compression structural design
**f_cr**: Characteristic flexural tensile strength (modulus of rupture)
**γ_m**: Partial safety factor for concrete material strength (Clause 36.4.2.1).
standards.notes: IS 456 strictly references 150mm cube strength as its baseline standard parameter.

standards.limits:
• **Specimen Standard**: Mapped as $$f_{ck,cyl} / f_{ck,cube}$$ (e.g., C25/30 = 25 MPa cylinder / 30 MPa cube).
• **Design Compressive Strength ($$f_{cd}$$)**: $$\alpha_{cc} f_{ck} / \gamma_C$$ where $$\alpha_{cc} = 0.85 - 1.0$$ and $$\gamma_C = 1.5$$.
• **Mean Axial Tensile Strength ($$f_{ctm}$$)**: $$0.30 \cdot f_{ck}^{(2/3)}$$ for $$\le C50/60$$.
• **Design Tensile Strength ($$f_{ctd}$$)**: $$\alpha_{ctd} f_{ctk,0.05} / \gamma_C$$.
standards.notation:
**f_ck**: Characteristic cylinder compressive strength ($$f_{ck,cyl}$$)
**f_ck,cube**: Characteristic 150mm cube strength
**f_cd**: Design compressive strength of concrete
**f_ctm**: Mean axial tensile strength of concrete (Table 3.1)
**α_cc**: Coefficient taking account of long term effects on compressive strength (Clause 3.1.6)
**γ_C**: Partial safety factor for concrete ($$1.5$$ for persistent/transient design situations).
standards.notes: Eurocode uses cylinder strength ($$f_{ck,cyl}$$) as the primary base input for design formulas.

standards.limits:
• **Specimen Standard**: 6x12 inch ($$150 \times 300$$ mm) Cylinder tested at 28 days ($$f'_c$$).
• **Design Strength**: Incorporates strength reduction factor ($\phi$) instead of material partial safety factor.
• **Modulus of Rupture ($$f_r$$)**: $$0.62 \lambda \sqrt{f'_c}$$ MPa ($$7.5 \lambda \sqrt{f'_c}$$ psi).
• **Modulus of Elasticity ($$E_c$$)**: $$4700 \sqrt{f'_c}$$ MPa ($$57,000 \sqrt{f'_c}$$ psi).
standards.notation:
**f'_c**: Specified characteristic compressive strength of concrete measured using standard cylinders
**f_r**: Modulus of rupture (tensile strength under flexure)
**ϕ**: Strength reduction factor ($$0.65 - 0.90$$ depending on member section failure mode per Section 21.2)
**λ**: Lightweight concrete modification factor (Section 19.2.4).
standards.notes: ACI 318 does not use structural material partial factors ($$\gamma_m$$); it scales capacities directly using overall section nominal reduction factors ($\phi$).

standards.limits:
• **Specimen Standard**: Standard Cylinder ($$f_{ck}$$). Cube equivalence defined via explicit conversion arrays.
• **Mean Compressive Strength ($$f_{cm}$$)**: $$f_{ck} + 8$$ MPa.
• **Mean Tensile Strength ($$f_{ctm}$$)**: $$0.30 \cdot (f_{ck})^{2/3}$$ for $$\le C50$$; $$2.12 \cdot \ln(1 + 0.1(f_{ck} + 8))$$ for $$> C50$$.
standards.notation:
**f_ck**: Characteristic cylinder compressive strength at 28 days
**f_cm**: Mean compressive strength of concrete
**Δf**: Margin offset stress equal to $$8\text{ MPa}$$
**f_ctm**: Mean axial tensile strength across extended performance curves.
standards.notes: Serves as the analytical baseline framework for material property derivations across global codes.
